reasoning: Preserved all seven failure-driven edits as the higher-priority corrective guidance. Added the distinct success-driven call-ordering insight because it does not conflict with or duplicate a failure edit. No edits target protected content.

edits.target: - Turn the query into a checklist of distinct requested outcomes, including each subject, action, and explicit constraint. Keep modifiers attached to the result they qualify. Match each outcome to an available endpoint by its actual operation and schema, not just a shared keyword; distinguish similar operations and prefer an explicitly named endpoint when available.
edits.content: - Turn the query into a checklist of distinct requested outcomes, including each subject, action, and explicit constraint. Keep modifiers attached to the result they qualify. Match each outcome to an endpoint that returns the requested kind and granularity of result, using its actual operation and schema rather than topical similarity (for example, distinguish item-level results from aggregate counts, and suggestions from pricing). Prefer an explicitly named endpoint when available. When the user names a platform or provider, treat it as a source constraint: use a matching endpoint from that source when it fulfills the request, rather than substituting another provider's generic endpoint. Treat narrative transitions as context, not as authorization for an additional operation.

edits.target: - Build the smallest complete call set: cover every requested outcome, and make every call serve one of them. Use one endpoint for multiple outcomes only when it genuinely covers them; make separate calls for distinct inputs unless the schema supports batching. If a requested endpoint is unavailable, use a listed alternative only if it genuinely fulfills the request. Do not invent tools, add unrelated calls, or include redundant alternatives or validators.
edits.content: - Build the smallest complete call set: cover every requested outcome, and make every call serve one of them. Before responding, trace each call to a requested outcome and verify that every outcome has a fulfilling call; remove calls with no corresponding outcome. If a documented filter captures the requested scope, use it on the relevant call rather than adding an unfiltered duplicate, unless the broader result is separately requested. Use one endpoint for multiple outcomes only when it genuinely covers them; make separate calls for distinct inputs unless the schema supports batching. If a requested endpoint is unavailable, use a listed alternative only if it genuinely fulfills the request. Do not invent tools, add unrelated calls, or include redundant alternatives or validators.

edits.target: - When calls are independent, issue them together rather than treating narrative order as a dependency.
edits.content: - Treat an explicit request to run, test, or execute code as a distinct outcome. If a code-execution endpoint is available, call it using its schema; when the computation is specified but code is not supplied, provide code that performs the requested computation rather than dropping that outcome.

edits.target: - Preserve requested search text, identifiers, and constraints; normalize only as the endpoint requires, without dropping meaningful words or substituting one value or geographic level for another. Map explicit filters, counts, pages, sorting, locale, category, and location to the corresponding schema fields, using accepted representations for enums and locales.
edits.content: - Preserve requested search text, identifiers, and constraints; normalize only as the endpoint requires, without dropping meaningful words or substituting one value or geographic level for another. Map explicit filters, counts, pages, sorting, locale, category, and location to the corresponding schema fields, using accepted representations for enums and locales. Do not infer filters merely from a named publisher, source, or subject's association.

edits.target: - Translate stated market constraints into API-native values according to the tool schema.
edits.content: - Translate stated market constraints into API-native values according to the tool schema. Keep each constraint scoped to its requested outcome and carry every compatible constraint into the call. Preserve both bounds of a stated range when corresponding minimum and maximum fields are available; preserve comparison direction and units (for example, map “at least” to a minimum and “at most” to a maximum, converting to the schema's units). For exact quantities, use an exact-value field or matching lower and upper bounds when supported. Map an exact requested result count, including one, to a supported count, limit, or page-size field; for paginated requests, map both the requested page and result count/page size when available. Select the date field corresponding to the event named in the request, and map semantic filters and sorting to documented API flags or enum values. Use the endpoint's accepted locale form and canonical enum, code, or slug; do not guess undocumented values or substitute a semantically different field when the requested distinction is unavailable.

edits.target: Represent parameters in the schema's required form and types. Put each in the declared required or optional bucket, and do not duplicate parameters across buckets. Include optional settings only when requested or clearly implied; use documented recency or freshness controls for requests such as “recent” or “latest,” and a modest supported result count when wording such as “some” calls for one. Do not invent dates, defaults, limits, IDs, credentials, filler values, or other unsupported constraints. If a required value is missing, do not fabricate it.
edits.content: For each selected endpoint, take parameter names, declared types, and required-versus-optional placement from that endpoint's own schema; do not borrow fields or bucket assignments from a similar endpoint. Put every required field in the required bucket and every non-required field in the optional bucket, even when the user explicitly requests an optional setting; never duplicate a field across buckets. Use the schema's declared types and accepted enum or API-native forms, including canonical codes, symbols, and casing, while preserving identifiers and free-text search wording. Include optional settings only when requested or clearly implied; use documented recency or freshness controls for requests such as “recent” or “latest,” and a modest supported result count when wording such as “some” calls for one. Do not invent dates, defaults, limits, IDs, credentials, filler values, or other unsupported constraints. If a required value is missing, do not fabricate it.

edits.target: - Check that every requested outcome is covered, each call uses the exact listed tool name, and each call object follows the active answer format exactly. Use the required keys, parameter buckets, types, and wrappers; include empty arrays when required. Do not merge calls, duplicate keys, or add explanatory text outside the required format.
edits.content: - Check that every requested outcome is covered and each call uses the exact canonical tool label shown in the tool list: copy the listed `Provider: endpoint` name verbatim, not its description or an alias, and do not add a second provider prefix. Verify that arguments use the schema's parameter names, types, and required or optional buckets. Ensure each call follows the active answer format exactly, with required keys, wrappers, and empty arrays when required; verify the final payload is syntactically valid with balanced delimiters. Do not merge calls, duplicate keys, or add explanatory text outside the required format.
- If the active answer format specifies an order for calls (for example, sorting by tool name), reorder the completed call objects to match it before responding; do not retain narrative task order.
